name: Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra
kicker: The sea-facing Quan The Am on Son Tra
summary: Ride the peninsula and walk up to Linh Ung. The Quan The Am is 67 meters and faces the sea from Bai But. No entry fee is published, so check on arrival if a gate asks. Allow half a day. The ride is the visit, not a stop on the way to dinner.
timeNeeded: Half a day with the ride
getThere: Bai But, about 10 km northeast of the center, by car or Grab.
heroCaption: The face and the raised hand of the Quan The Am

notice.title: No entry fee is published
notice.body: The city portal and the 2017 recognition state no fee. If a gate asks for one, check it on arrival. Do not budget a number this page does not have.

body: The pagoda is at Bai But, on the Son Tra peninsula. Ride out, then walk the terrace. The Quan The Am stands 67 meters, on a lotus pedestal 35 meters across, facing the sea. The pagoda’s own page says the site is about 10 kilometers northeast of the center and that it opened on 30 July 2010.

You walk up through the gate and the stair before you are under the statue. The peninsula road is the rest of the half-day. Do not treat the visit as a short stop between the beach and dinner, and do not ride a loop you do not know in the rain.
No entry fee is on the city portal, and the decision that recognized the site on 6 June 2017 states none either. A gate fee, if someone charges one, is check on arrival. No gate hour is published.

figures.caption: The gate and the stair up to the terrace
figures.alt: The ornate gate and stone stair at Linh Ung Pagoda on the Son Tra peninsula

gettingThere: Linh Ung is at Bai But, on the Son Tra peninsula. The pagoda’s English page says about 10 kilometers northeast of the center. Go by car or Grab. It is not a walk from My Khe unless you are already on that shore. A minute count beyond the distance is check on arrival.
